:::info

La documentación de esta integración la escribe su autor y, por ahora, solo está disponible en inglés.

Unofficial integration, not affiliated with Pure Energie nor NET2GRID. It
reads the **energy meter reader of Pure Energie** (a NET2GRID SmartBridge,
such as the SBWF3102, plugged on the P1 port of your electricity meter)
through its local HTTP API: no cloud, no account, no key, nothing sent to the
device but read requests (GET), one read every 30 seconds at most.

**Never tested with a real device**: it was built from the Python library
gridnet (the one the Pure Energie integration of Home Assistant uses).
Feedback welcome.

## What you get

One device, named after the model and the end of the id of the meter reader
(`Pure Energie SBWF3102 3795`):

| Feature               | Kind              |
| --------------------- | ----------------- |
| Power                 | energy sensor, W  |
| Consumption index     | energy index, kWh |
| Injection index (kWh) | plain sensor      |

- The **power** is signed: below 0 while your home injects (solar panels).
- The **consumption index** feeds the Gladys energy monitoring: Gladys
  derives the consumption and its cost from it. It is published once a minute
  at most and checked first: a value of 0 is never sent; any drop, even of
  1 Wh, or a jump larger than your home could have drawn (the "highest
  plausible power" of the configuration, 100 kW by default, over the time
  since the last value) is **held back** (the last accepted value is sent
  again) and shown in the integration status. If it is right (a new meter),
  click **Accept the held index** twice (see Buttons). Saving the
  configuration never accepts it.
- The **injection** is never in the energy monitoring (it would be billed as
  consumption): a plain sensor, never sent at 0.
- An index given in another unit than Wh or kWh, or without a unit, is not
  sent (the status says so): an index is never guessed.
- Gas is not read.

## Fresh values only

The meter reader dates its values. A read whose date and values have not
moved since the read before sends nothing: an old value is never sent as a
new one, not after a restart of the integration nor after a restart of
Gladys either (this mark is kept in `/data` for the 8 meter readers whose
values changed most recently: at the 9th, the oldest mark is forgotten, and a
reader that comes back frozen after a restart may then be published once; also
when the clock of Gladys restarts behind it). When nothing has moved
for 2 hours, the status says so. Without a date, a fingerprint of the
values stands for it.

## Identity

The device is keyed by the id the meter reader gives on its `/info` page
(`84df:0c11:9999:3795`, kept as its hex digits). Every read asks for the id
before and after the values: if another id answers in between, or if the id
cannot be read, nothing from that read is published. If another meter reader
answers at the address, it gets its own device (create it in Discover); the
old device keeps its history.

## Setup

1. Find the IP address of the meter reader in your router, and preferably
   give it a fixed address there.
2. In Gladys, open the integration, enter this address and save.
3. In the **Discover** tab, create the device.

## Buttons

- **Test the connection**: reads the meter reader once when a read is due
  (never more than one every 30 seconds), otherwise tells the last read: its
  id, the power, the consumption and injection indexes.
- **Accept the held index**, in two clicks. The first click shows the index
  held back and takes nothing. The second click, a few seconds to 5 minutes
  later, takes what the first showed, only if the held value has not changed
  since (beyond what the meter may have measured meanwhile). A jump is
  counted at once as consumption; a drop bills nothing.

## When something goes wrong

- **Unreachable or wrong answer**: new try after 30 seconds, then doubled up
  to 10 minutes.
- **The device asks to wait (429) or fails (5xx)**: reads paused from 1
  minute to 6 hours, also after a restart.
- **The state file in `/data` cannot be read**: it is left as it is (never
  written over) and the status says so; a held index or the date of the last
  values may then be forgotten.

## Privacy

Everything stays on your network. The integration only sends GET requests to
the address you entered.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Pure Energie te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Pure Energie meter reader | `section` | No | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Pure Energie nor NET2GRID. It reads the energy meter reader of Pure Energie (a NET2GRID SmartBridge, plugged on the P1 port of the electricity meter) through its local HTTP API, without any cloud nor key: the power every 30 seconds (signed: below 0 while you inject), the consumption index once a minute for the Gladys energy monitoring, and the injection index as a plain sensor. Read-only. Gas is not read. Never tested with a real device. |
| Meter reader address | `string` | Sí | The IP address of the meter reader on your network (shown by your router), with a port only if it is not 80. Preferably give it a fixed address in your router; if it changes, enter the new one: the device keeps its history (it is keyed by the id of the meter reader). |
| Highest plausible power of the home (kW) | `number` | No | The guard of the consumption index holds back a rise larger than this power over the time since the last value (100 kW by default). |

## Cómo instalar Pure Energie en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Pure Energie aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-pure-energie:0.1.2`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-pure-energie](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-pure-energie).

Pure Energie requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Pure Energie es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
